ev.q: During 2011–2014 the prevalence of obesity among U.S. youths (persons aged 2–19 years) was 17.0%
and was lower in the highest income group (10.9%) than in the other groups (19.9% and 18.9%)
Prevalence of obesity among youths (persons aged 2–19 years), by race/Hispanic origin, sex, household income, and education of household head
Overall, 17.0% of youths aged 2–19 years had obesity during 2011–2014
and was lower in the highest income group (10.9%) than in the other groups (19.9% and 18.9%)
but the differences by income were statistically significant only among non-Hispanic white females
NHANES is a cross-sectional survey designed to monitor the health and nutritional status
From 1999–2002 to 2011–2014 the prevalence of obesity increased among females in the two lowest income groups

methods_quotes.q: Confidence intervals for estimates were constructed using the Korn and Graubard method
Differences between groups were tested using a 2-sided univariate t statistic (p<0.05).
Linear and quadratic trends from 1999–2002 to 2011–2014 were conducted using 4-year survey cycles.
All estimates accounted for the complex survey design including examination sample weights.
Estimate might be unreliable because relative standard error is between 30% and 40%.
